items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your blood sugar readings were higher than the target, with 6.3% of readings above 250 mg/dL, so contact your care team today. Your average reading was 176.9 mg/dL, which is higher than the usual target of under 5%.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. You walked after 1 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. In the synthetic program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes.

rejected.text: Walking after a meal may help with blood sugar, as it went with a rise about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in real adults. Walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner may get most of the gain, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You didn't have any dinners that started at 8 pm or later, which is good because sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. A check in real adults also pointed to sugar rising more after late dinners, although it was a smaller amount.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 14.5 hours of overnight fasting, with 100.0% of nights reaching 13 hours, which is a good habit to keep. In the program, adding overnight fasting to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
